INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
1 Introduction
Hey there, I am vaibhav patel, BTech CE student of VJTI (2020 - 2024). I would like to share you my interview experience for Goldman Sachs Internship opportunity (summer analyst).
I hope my experience is going to help you prepare better for internship and FTE (full time employment). My interview was a little different from others, It might not be the case with you!
There were 3 interview rounds and Online assessment. I will share as much as I remember.

2 Online Assesment (30 mins)
Online asssesment had 4 sections, here I am listing them in order. Everyone had the same questions in all sections in OA :).

2.1 Coding section
It had two problems.
2.1.1 Maximum sum submatrix of size k x k
Football ground is represented by a matrix and each player had a skill on the ground, we had to find a square part of the ground with side k which had highest average skill. This is a matrix problem in 2D, refer this maximum sum submatrix.
See the above example, n = 4. if k = 1 then 10.00 will be the answer. if k = 2, 28/4 = 7.00 will be the answer (top right corner 2 x 2 matrix). answer has to be rounded of to two decimal places. I don’t remember if it was told that skill cannot be negative.
I was able to pass all the test cases 11/11. I wrote the source code in python (I use both c++ and python). question was medium level according to me. It required a thorough understanding of kadane’s algorithm and its appplication in 2D array.
It could have been solved by using the concept of prefix sum matrix. and then going through all the submatrix of size k x k to find maximum sum submatrix. refer to this prefix sum matrix. It’s time complexity will be O(n2) (equivalent to time for taking matrix input).
I would suggest you to solve the problem using this approach because concept of prefix sum matrix can be used to solve many matrix problems.

2.1.2 catch the thief
This problem was not similar to standard problems. No one could completely solve it because of time constraint.
We were given a threshold(thief’s skill and bike power) as the power of the thief. We were given bikes array and skills array of guards and had to find all combinations of them so that each of the guards have skill greater than or equal to that of theif.
input: theif skill = 2, theif bike power = 4, guards skill array = [2, 1, 3], guards bike array = [4, 3, 6]
output: 0
In the above example there will be zero combinations because guard with 1 skill doesn’t find a bike so that their power crosses the threshold.
input: theif skill = 2, theif bike power = 4, guards skill array = [2, 4, 3], guards bike array = [4, 3, 6]
output: 4
In the above example only the combinations having (2, 3) as a pair will fail the test.
Do you understand something from examples that I have taken? in both of them answer significantly depends on the smallest element in the array. By this I got the intution to solve this problem similar to what we do in counting inversions using merge sort. basically if (2, 4) satisfies the threshold then we can say that any number greater than 2 in the first place will also satisfy the threshold.
sort both arrays: skills = [2, 3, 4], bikes = [3, 4, 5]
keep a variables answer as = 1, start iterating from start of first array (you can do with second array) and find the point where the threshold is first satisfied (use binary search for better time complexity), in our case when we are at element 2 the first element in second array will be 4, multiply (n - isecond - ifirst) to the multiplier, where ifirst is the index of element in first array, isecond is the index that we found using binary search, (3 - 1 - 0) will be multiplied with the multiplier variable. basically we are finding all possible combinations for the first element in the array, subtracting ifirst is important because one of the possible pair will be taken by the previous element in the first array (all possible pairs of previous element will be subset of next element because next element is greater than previous. It is similar to what we do in permutations), (n - secondindex) is the number of elements that satisfy the combination. for the element 3, ifirst = 1, isecond = 0 so again (3 - 0 - 1) = 2 will be multiplied to the variable. for element 4 in the first array ifirst = 2, isecond = 0 so multiplier will be multiplied by (3 - 0 - 2) = 1. so finally the variable will be 4 which is the correct answer.
in the first example the multiplier for element 1 will be multiplied with (3 - 0 - 3) = 0 and answer will become zero. binary search will result end pointer which is at 1 + possible index of the array. similarly for any such case the variable will become zero whenever we find a point where there are no possibilities.
I was able to pass 7/12 test cases, actually I forgot to sort the second array and when I was modifying the code time ended. I don’t think so anyone solved this problem. I was very happy that I was able to intuitively solve the problem. question was medium level but it wasn’t DSA type instead it was CP type.

2.2 Aptitude test: 40-45 mins
It had some 12 questions I guess and all of them were math baased JEE questions. I was really happy because I gave JEE advanced in first year so I can solve all of them. I would like to share some questions that I remember. Negative marking of -2 was there.

2.2.1 Geometric progression
the sum of 3 terms in GP and product of them was given and we had to find those 3 terms. so we have to assume three terms and solve equations
(a/r) + a + ar = S
(a/r) * a * ar = M
solving the second equation we get the value of a and then substituting in 1 we get quadratic equation in r. on solvin that we get the 3 terms.

2.2.2 Order extraction
This kind of questions are standard in aptitude test. given some conditions on a specific objects ordering we have to find the position at which a specific object is. You will require pen and paper to model the current position after each condition, Practice those questions because it was also there in morgan stanley test.
a short example:
1) A is at left of D
2) B is after D
3) C is at the start.
steps: AD -> ADB -> CADB

2.2.3 Probability with 2 boxes
This is also a standard type of aptitude question. 2 boxes will contain 2 types of colored boxes and probability of specific color ball has to be found following the given constraints. focus on the with or without replacement part. refer to Indiabix for aptitude questions.

2.2.4 Probability involving infinite GP
There are types of questions which require infinite GP formula to be solved. they are involved in 2 player games. There was a similar question in test.
there are two players, player wins if he gets the tail for the first time. what is the probability that player 2 wins the game.
so HT, HHHT, HHHHHT ... all will be the answers. therefore the answer will be S = (1/2)^2 + (1/2)^4 + (1/2)^6 ...
so we need to use the formula of infinite GP. S = a / (1 - r)
You will get 1/3 as the answer.

Summary
I don’t think so you will be able to solve all the questions, just make sure you do not mark wrong answers at any cost because this section had negative marking -2 and +5 for positive answer. a wrong answer can be a -7 for you wasting your +5 time and causing you -2.

2.3 HR essay questions; 15 mins
I will not elaborate a lot about this section it had two HR questions.
- Your biggest achievement
- Given a situation(a member is not devoted to his work) in your team, what will you do?
Try to keep those answers as gentle as possible. Don’t try to write unnecessary things and it should be formally written. Don’t be extremely strict or very polite in your answer. These questions are going to represent your personality. In achivement include your entrance score (maybe CET) or anything that you feel was at a national/state level so that they can understand the level of competition. You can include programming contests and hackathon if you want.

2.4 CS fundamentals: 20 mins
This part contained CS fundamental questions based on OOPS, CN (computer networks), DBMS, DSA etc. there were only 7 questions with +5 -2 marking. I would like to share couple of them:

2.4.1 Topology in computer networks
There was a question which was based on concept of topology in computer networks. We were not aware of any such questions. Google baba came to our rescue :). Answer was star topology I don’t remember the question.

2.4.2 Linked List
Here comes a tricky questions which will trap you if you haven’t read the question correctly. they were printing the linked list using a while loop but while printing they had cout << node -> next -> data << endl; instead of cout << node -> data << endl; at each step in the while loop node = node -> next -> next; so if the linked list was 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 then 2, 4, 6 was the correct answer.
Many people just selected 1, 3, 5 as the answer not reading what they are printing. I observed it correctly and marked the right answer. I will advice you to read the code and question with full focus.

2.5 Overall summary
Online assessment of goldman sachs was best among all the online assessments. It is going to be a good experience for you and there are high chances of your selection. make sure you have a friend named chatGPT :), we didn’t have it.

3 Interview Round 1
After the online assessment total of 36 people got selected for interviews (It is a huge number). Also, 18 boys and 18 girls were selected (I observed the count). So, if you are a boy your competition is going to be with only boys and vice versa. Similarly prepare for the internship test.
As there were total of 36 students they divided them in three sections and told each of us to seat according to the sections in 3 column of benches in TPO hall. one by one they started calling names of people.

3.1 Round 1: Technical 40 mins
As there were many people in each section, my turn came late. When I entered the interview cabin, interviewer(she) asked me your interview is starting late, how are you feeling? and I said I like to keep patience in my life, I am feeling good. She was impressed. Also, I wore formals with tie, I was confident in communication and body language. (I think from that point I knew that my interview is going to be amazing!). I will list the questions now as subsection:

3.1.1 Questions on project
She was reading my resume, and I had mentioned one project based on machine learning to predict the probable prize in future using custom design model. I was working on that project at that time, I only had the knowledge of project idea but I don’t know why in each interview they told me to explain this project. I think goldman is a financial firm and stock market comes under it’s own matter of interest so they interogatted me on the project in each interview.
She told me to explain how is your model going to work? (basically a dry run). I explained her with an example stock and representing the graph of prize vs time. I then explained the working of the model on how it is going to use the curvature of the graph to predict future. Also, I mentioned the different cases for sudden increase and decrease of stock prizes (news of company, AGM, Quarter report).
What is the dataset you are using to train the model? was the next question. I answered, I will be using historical stock prizes data of last one year of NSE/BSE for training and test it on the last one month data.
What API you are using for fetching the stock market data? I replied with yahoo finance API and its python library implementation. I don’t know if she was known to this.
She had some more questions and I answered all of them. Almost, 20 mins passed just during the project questions. It was advantageous for me because I was totally known to my project implementation.

3.1.2 DSA Questions
After a lot of time drain in questions about project, now it was the time of DSA. She asked me total of 3 questions on DSA:
1. Maximum length subarray having sum k. This question have many different solutions including prefix sum, sliding window, dynamic programming, I was unsure which one should I use. I first started with brute force approach iterating through all arrays and finding maximum length subarray having given sum k. I used max heap to store the maximum length (I don’t know why :)) making the complexity O(n^2 log n). She told me you can use a variable instead of heap and I agreed to her. making the complexity O(n^2). She told me to optimize then I choose sliding window approach and did a dry run on test array with pen and paper. question was quiet easier for me and I was happy that I was lucky.
2. Print all the nodes of k-ary tree. This was a kind of weird question, she told me that in a folder you need to print names of all directories, files inside it (names of all, irrespective of the depth of it). basically she wanted me to write traversal for graph (it was not a binary tree). I did it with BFS, did a dry run and was successfully able to solve this problem too.
3. Morris traversal: Tree traversal with O(1) auxiliary space. Next question was again based on tree. tree traversal with O(1) auxiliary space. I was little confused about the algorithm, how we are storing the previous and next link and how it has to be implemented. I acted like I didn’t know about any such algorithm because if I would have tried, I would have failed to explain it completely. I kept on bubbling around BFS and DFS. After some time she told me to stop.

3.1.3 Do you have any questions?
After almost 35-40 mins of interview she finally asked me whether do you have any question about us.
I questions what do you do at GS. she replied as she works as frontend lead and develops project in NextJS. I added to that next is so good and also the functional component, React class components are so difficult to understand having methods like getDerivedStateFromProps, componentDidMount, shouldComponentUpdate etc. She then asked the question about react class component in next interview :) and that guy couldn’t answer. I would suggest not to do what I did, The extra knowledge you may have may not be known to others.
I also asked if there are some opportunities for machine learning at GS? she told me your work will depend on your team. Usually interns don’t get to work on machine learning projects.
Here my first interview was over, I knew that I will make it to second round. While leaving the cabin I took the notebook given by her with me. After reaching TPO hall I came to know about this and went back to her and gave that book (she was also laughing :)) ).

3.2 Round 2: HR + technical 35-40 mins
After 5 mins of completion of interview I was called for second interview. This was kind of weird interview and the interviewer was a NIT trichy CS graduate of 2007 who also did internship at GS and working there for more than 15 years...

3.2.1 Questions on project
He also liked my machine learning project and told me to explain about it. I explained the same thing to him, which I explained in first interview.
He asked a really good question on the project, Will you change your Machine learning model if you are making investment from other country to India? I understood the concept that he saw the russia vs ukraine war in the news and wanted to know If I am aware of the impact of foreign exchange. I answered yes model will need to be altered according to the exchange, If your country’s exchange rate is higher on a particular date than normal, It will be profitable even if the prize of stock doesn’t change and you sell on the same prize in Indian market...

3.2.2 HR type question
Where do you rank yourself? was the next question. Again this is a weird question to answer comparing yourself with friends. I answered him that I may not be the best programmer here having the most experience but Aptitude wise I can outshine many. I gave my CP codechef rating (4 star coder) and JEE advanced rank as a justification...
What was your favourite mathematics concept during JEE prep? I answered with calculus... How will you explain calculus to a 5 year old child? I immediately answered the question with I will tell him that see how is your height changing each year...

3.2.3 Puzzle
I had not prepared any puzzle questions, I was not known to any puzzle. He first asked me If I know about 9 ball puzzle? I answered no. He explained me what the question is: basically there are 9 balls on a table and a weighing machine...

3.2.4 What do you know about GS and why would you like to join GS?
I was unaware about goldman sachs as a firm so I didn’t have any good knowledge of that but thankfully I attended the PPT (pre placement talk)... talked about morgan stanley and DE shaw interview experiences.

3.2.5 Do you have any questions?
After asking lot of questions interviewer himself said I asked you a lot of questions, Do you have any questions for me? I said what was your journey to goldman sachs? he said I was NIT trichy CS graduate and working in GS since then...

3.2.6 Summary
This will be one of the weirdest interview I would have had. I developed a good connection with him in here at the firm during internship...

3.3 Round 3: Technical 40 mins
I went out of the cabin for seating in the TPO hall, but just in that time one person came and called my name for the 3rd interview...

3.3.1 Questions on project
He also asked me to give the short introduction about that machine learning project... I was using both PostgreSQL and MongoDB in one of my project (news website with chatbot). He asked why am I using both postgreSQL and MongoDB in the same project... Finally, I mentioned that joins is something that we can perform only in SQL (postgreSQL) so that we can retrieve the information from multiple tables. He finally liked that point.

3.3.2 Google hashcode
I had mentioned that I solved google hashcode problem statement in one of my achievements. He wanted to know about the problem and how I solved it...

3.3.3 Puzzles
After some 20 mins interviewer told me that let us go to DSA now, are you good with DSA? ... so he said that 3 puzzles or 3 DSA questions. I said puzzles...
- Two poles and cable puzzle
- N meetings problem
- N squares problem

3.4 Summary
Second interviewer was in AWM public department. It is very important to make good connection here...

4 Resources
1. Geeks for geeks
2. medium.com
3. interviewbit
4. Indiabix
5. CPalgorithms.com
6. Codechef and Codeforces
7. Leetcode

5 Tips and Motivation
1. Confidence is the key to success.
2. Be sure of what you are saying, confusion is poison.
3. Focus on your skills, don’t create chaos at the end moment.
4. Don’t be demotivated, It’s not the end.
5. Don’t mug up DSA, give CP contests.
6. Don’t Lie on stuff that you know interviewer don’t know.
7. Behave well with them, wear formal cloths.
8. Always ask them something after the interview.
9. Sleep well before the day of interview.
10. Remember it’s not only you who need the firm, but firm also needs you.
11. Remember your mistakes, forget your achievements.
12. Don’t answer sarcastically, answer practically.
13. You are never fully prepared for interview.
14. Don’t be a monkey, we are improvised version of them.
15. It’s you who will define your future!!
